en: n. a line that bends smoothly without any sharp angles; a bend in a road or river; a pitch in baseball that curves; vt. to make something bend; vi. to bend in a smooth line
ex: The road takes a sharp curve to the left near the bridge.
道路在橋附近急轉向左彎。

en: vt. to change something completely, especially to improve it; to change the form of something; vi. to change completely
ex: The new technology will transform the way we work.
這項新技術將徹底改變我們工作的方式。

en: n. a sudden loud noise and violent release of energy; a sudden large increase in something; a sudden outburst of strong feeling
ex: The explosion shook all the buildings on the street.
爆炸震動了街上所有的建築。

en: a. able to bend easily without breaking; able to change easily to suit new conditions; willing to change or compromise
ex: We offer flexible working hours to all employees.
我們為所有員工提供彈性工時。

en: n. something that you say or write that gives your opinion about something; a note that explains something in a text; vi. to say or write something that expresses your opinion
ex: She made a rude comment about my clothes.
她對我的衣服說了不禮貌的話。

en: vi. to be different from something else; to disagree with someone
ex: Opinions differ on how to solve the problem.
對於如何解決這個問題，意見不一。

en: n. things that are made to be sold; possessions that belong to someone; items transported by rail or road
ex: The store sells a wide range of household goods.
這家店販售各式各樣的家用商品。

en: n. a close-fitting covering for the feet and legs, usually made of nylon or silk
ex: She wore black stockings with her dress.
她穿著洋裝搭配黑色長襪。

en: a. having no result or effect; too proud of your own appearance or abilities; of no value
ex: She made a vain attempt to open the locked door.
她徒勞地想打開那扇鎖著的門。

en: vt. to make something happen sooner or faster; vi. to hurry to do something
ex: The bad weather hastened our departure.
壞天氣促使我們提早出發。

en: n. a glass container or building in which fish and other water animals are kept; a place where people can go to see these animals
ex: The kids loved watching the colorful fish at the aquarium.
孩子們喜歡在水族館看色彩繽紛的魚。

en: vt. to suffer something painful or difficult for a long time without giving up; to accept something unpleasant; vi. to continue to exist for a long time
ex: She endured the pain without complaining.
她忍受著疼痛，沒有抱怨。

en: n. the quality of being faithful to a person, group or principle; a strong feeling of support or allegiance
ex: The dog showed great loyalty to its owner.
那隻狗對主人展現出極大的忠誠。

en: adv. to a great degree; mainly; on a large scale
ex: The city's population is largely made up of young people.
這座城市的人口主要由年輕人組成。

en: v. to tell someone angrily that they have done something wrong; n. a person who often criticizes others loudly
ex: His mother scolded him for coming home late.
他媽媽因為他很晚回家而罵了他。

en: n. the ability to understand something immediately without needing to think about it or have proof; a feeling that something is true without knowing why
ex: Her intuition told her that something was wrong.
她的直覺告訴她事情不對勁。

en: a. relating to athletes or sports; physically strong and good at sports
ex: He has an athletic build because he plays basketball every day.
他每天打籃球，所以體格健壯。

en: n. a strong alcoholic drink such as whisky or vodka; a liquid, especially one that results from cooking; vt. to soak something in a liquid
ex: He is not allowed to drink liquor because he is underage.
他未成年，不可以喝酒。

en: n. the act of changing something to improve it; a changed version of something; the act of reviewing work to prepare for an exam
ex: The professor asked me to make a few revisions to my paper.
教授要我對論文做一些修改。

en: n. a feeling of pity and sadness for someone who is experiencing something bad; agreement with someone's ideas or aims; words of comfort for someone who has suffered a loss
ex: I have a great deal of sympathy for people who lose their jobs.
我對失業的人深表同情。

en: n. the largest amount or highest level that is possible; a. as large or as great as possible
ex: The maximum speed on this road is 80 kilometers per hour.
這條路的最高時速是八十公里。

en: a. covered with or full of mud; (of liquid) not clear; not clear or well defined; vt. to make something dirty with mud; to make something unclear
ex: Don't walk into the house with your muddy shoes.
別穿著沾滿泥巴的鞋子走進屋子。

en: v. to move quickly to avoid something or someone; to avoid doing something that you should do; n. a clever way of avoiding something; a trick
ex: He dodged the ball and ran to the other side of the field.
他閃過球，跑到球場另一邊。

en: n. a simple drawing that shows the parts or workings of something; a plan or sketch that explains how something works
ex: The teacher drew a diagram to explain how the heart works.
老師畫了一張圖解釋心臟如何運作。

en: vt. to put money into something in order to make a profit; to spend time or effort on something; to give someone power or rank; vi. to put money into a business or other thing
ex: He invested all his savings in the stock market.
他把所有積蓄都投資在股市。

en: vi. to work together with other people to achieve something; to be willing to help someone
ex: The two companies agreed to cooperate on the new project.
兩家公司同意就這項新專案合作。

en: n. a person who studies the meaning of life, knowledge and ideas; a person who has a calm attitude towards life
ex: Socrates was one of the most famous philosophers in history.
蘇格拉底是歷史上最著名的哲學家之一。

en: n. a person who has been forced to leave their country because of war, persecution or natural disaster
ex: Thousands of refugees crossed the border to escape the war.
數千名難民越過邊境逃離戰爭。

en: vt. to provide a room or building with furniture; to supply something that is needed; to give information
ex: They furnished the new apartment with modern furniture.
他們用現代傢俱布置了新公寓。

en: vt. to interrupt someone while they are doing something; to make someone feel worried or upset; to change the normal arrangement or condition of something
ex: Please don't disturb me while I'm studying.
我念書的時候請不要打擾我。

en: n. a signal for someone to do something, especially to start speaking or acting; something that serves as a hint or reminder; a long stick used to hit the ball in billiards; vt. to give someone a signal to do something
ex: She waited for her cue before walking on stage.
她等待提示後才走上舞台。

en: n. a prayer or wish for good fortune or happiness; something that brings happiness or good luck; approval or support for something
ex: It was a blessing that no one was hurt in the accident.
沒有人在這場意外中受傷，真是萬幸。

en: a. very beautiful, impressive or grand; of very high quality; excellent
ex: From the top of the hill, we saw a magnificent view of the valley.
我們從山頂看見山谷壯麗的景色。

en: a. absolutely necessary; extremely important; the basic or most important part of something; n. something that is absolutely necessary
ex: Water is essential for all living things.
水對所有生物都是必需的。

en: vt. to give something, especially money, to help achieve something; to write articles for a newspaper or magazine; vi. to help to make something happen
ex: Everyone can contribute to protecting the environment.
每個人都能為保護環境盡一份力。

en: n. the curved path of a planet, moon or satellite around another body; the area of influence of someone or something; the bony hole that holds the eye; vt. to travel in a circle around something; vi. to move in an orbit
ex: The satellite orbits the Earth every ninety minutes.
這顆衛星每九十分鐘繞地球一圈。

en: a. feeling or showing pity for someone; showing agreement with an idea or aim; n. a part of the nervous system
ex: She gave him a sympathetic smile when she heard the bad news.
她聽到壞消息時給了他一個同情的微笑。

en: vt. to explain the meaning of something; to understand something in a particular way; to perform a piece of music or a role in a way that expresses your own ideas; vi. to translate what someone says into another language
ex: How do you interpret this poem?
你如何詮釋這首詩？

en: n. a group of animals or plants that are similar and can breed together; a type or kind of something
ex: The panda is an endangered species.
貓熊是瀕臨絕種的物種。

en: vt. to explain or make something clear by using examples, pictures or stories; to draw pictures for a book; vi. to give examples to explain something
ex: The teacher used a diagram to illustrate her point.
老師用一張圖解說明她的論點。
